entries.definition: General name for anything an identity can hold or request: an entitlement, an access profile, a role, or an application grouping access for request.
A bundle of one or more entitlements that all come from a single source, usually made requestable with its own approval steps; unlike a role, it cannot span several sources.
An ask, made in Request Center or through the API, to grant or remove a role, access profile or entitlement for oneself or others, routed through configured approvers before changes happen.
A short-lived credential issued by an authorization server and presented as a bearer value on API calls; whoever holds it can use it until it expires.
A record of a user's login or presence on one connected system, collected by aggregation and, once matched, linked to exactly one identity in the tenant.
The record of an operation affecting accounts, such as a request, refresh, revocation or lifecycle change, listing each provisioning step and its success or failure for troubleshooting.
The job that reads every user record and its schema attributes from a connected system, then matches each to an owner; on authoritative sources it can create new identities.
A safeguard that stops an aggregation when more than a set percentage of existing accounts, 10 percent by default, would be removed, protecting against a truncated file or bad query.
The definition of which attributes a system returns for each account, including the unique key and display attribute; only listed attributes are stored in the cloud, limiting data sent.
Reads a named attribute from a person's account on a specified source, optionally choosing among several accounts, as input for further data processing.
Integration that reads and writes Microsoft directory users and groups over LDAP from the appliance, relying on IQService for password resets, Exchange mailboxes and PowerShell native rules.

Logic run once a target has processed a change; in Identity Security Cloud this is done with connector-side after-operation rules, such as an AD after-create PowerShell script via IQService, not a cloud rule.
Pulling account or group data from a connected system into the tenant on a schedule or on demand, followed by correlation and a refresh of affected identities.
An OAuth client registered by an administrator with chosen grant types, scopes and token lifetimes, used for system integrations that should not depend on any one person's login.
The single front door for REST calls to a tenant, at its api subdomain, which validates OAuth tokens and routes each call to the correct back-end microservice.
Files under the sailpoint user's log directory on a VA, chiefly ccg.log, examined to diagnose connection, collection and provisioning errors or to send to SailPoint support.
A user-facing tile in Request Center that groups requestable access profiles for one system under a friendly name and icon, so people find access by business name.
The ordered list of approvers, such as manager, owner, source owner, application owner or a governance group, that a request must pass through one after another before access is granted.
A signed statement issued by the system that verified a user, telling an application who the user is and sometimes their attributes, so the application can trust the sign-in.
The design in which cloud services and appliances exchange work through queued messages that the appliance polls for outbound, so jobs and results survive brief network or service outages.
Cloud-run code called from a create or update provisioning policy to compute an account value, such as a unique username, when transforms and built-in generators cannot express the logic.
A feature that pushes changes in identity attributes, such as a new department or surname, out to mapped account attributes on target systems so they stay consistent with authoritative data.
A record of something that happened in the tenant, such as a login, access request, provisioning change or configuration edit, kept for searching during audits and troubleshooting.
Proving that a user or service is who it claims to be, using passwords, keys, tokens or multiple factors, as distinct from deciding what it may do afterward.
A system of record, usually HR, whose accounts create identities and supply core data such as name, manager and hire date; each identity profile points at exactly one.
Deciding what an already-verified user or service is permitted to see or do, based on assigned rights, roles or policies; it follows proving who the caller is.
The OAuth 2.0 flow in which a person signs in through a browser and the application swaps the returned short-lived code for tokens, so it can act on that person's behalf.
A lightweight Java scripting language, interpreted at runtime with Java syntax and libraries, in which most SailPoint customization code is written.
Cloud-run code that inspects and modifies the provisioning plan just before it goes to the connector, for example adding a disable step or moving an account to another OU.
Endpoints published under the beta path that offer newer capabilities which may change or be removed without notice, unlike the stable versioned endpoints recommended for production scripts.
Baseline access granted automatically to everyone matching broad criteria, such as an email box and directory account for all employees, usually delivered by lifecycle states or criteria-based roles.
Appliance-side code run for each row during collection from delimited-file or database systems, reshaping raw columns into the attribute map stored for each account.
Criteria that exclude specific identities, access items or sources from a review campaign so reviewers see only relevant items and are not overloaded.
An administrative level allowed to create, launch, manage and monitor review campaigns without wider tenant configuration rights.
A time-boxed review in which designated reviewers confirm or revoke the access people hold, producing audit evidence; types include manager, source owner, search and role composition.
A reviewer forwarding selected review items to someone better placed to decide, such as a colleague who knows the system, while the campaign continues.
The final reviewer action that locks a campaign's decisions once every item is approved or revoked, after which revoked access is sent for removal; unsigned reviews do not remediate.
The OAuth 2.0 grant where a program trades a client ID and secret directly for an access token with no interactive sign-in, used by personal tokens and admin-created API clients.
An appliance's system time falling out of step with real time; it breaks token and TLS validation and makes the appliance appear disconnected until time synchronization is fixed.
The container on each appliance that runs connector code, carries out collections and account changes for the cloud, and writes the main log reviewed during troubleshooting.

Custom code that executes inside SailPoint's cloud, such as correlation, identity attribute or before provisioning logic; it must be submitted to SailPoint for review and deployment, unlike appliance-side connector code.
The special identity attribute, usually calculated by a transform from HR dates or status, whose value decides which employment stage a person is in and therefore which actions run.
Meeting regulatory and audit obligations such as SOX, HIPAA or GDPR by proving who has access, how it was approved and that it is reviewed regularly.
Joins an ordered array of strings and nested results into one string, for instance building a display name from first name, a space and last name.
Evaluates a simple equality expression between two values and returns one result when it is true and another when false, such as setting a flag only for one location.
The file placed on a new appliance during setup that holds the pairing details, tenant API address and key passphrase it needs to register with its cluster.
A point-in-time JSON snapshot of selected tenant objects that can later be reviewed as a draft and restored or uploaded, protecting against harmful changes and supporting migrations.
The tool for backing up, comparing and restoring tenant configuration objects such as sources, transforms, roles and workflows, and for moving them between tenants like sandbox and production.
The integration component that speaks a target system's protocol or API, letting the tenant read accounts and groups and perform create, modify, disable and delete operations.

Custom code that executes on the virtual appliance within a connector, such as a JDBC build map or web services after-operation step; customers upload it through the API after validation, without SailPoint review.
Matching each collected account to the identity that owns it by comparing configured attribute pairs, such as employee number to employeeId, or by a cloud rule when simple comparison fails.
Cloud-run code used during aggregation when attribute-pair matching cannot link accounts to people; it returns the identity attribute and value that identify each account's owner.
The provisioning policy on a source listing which attributes, with values from identity data, transforms or generators, are set when a new account is made there.
Access granted because an identity matches a role's conditions; when attributes change and the match ends, a later refresh removes the role and its access, unlike a requested assignment.
Compares two dates with operators such as greater than or less than and returns a chosen value, often used to set employment stages from hire or termination dates.
Converts a date string between formats, for example from an HR system's MM/dd/yyyy text to ISO8601, so date comparisons and lifecycle logic work reliably.
A system whose account and group data are uploaded as CSV files rather than read live; changes for it are handed to people as manual work items.
Collection that retrieves only records changed since the last run, using change tracking on the target such as directory change markers; faster than a full run, which reads everything.
An integration that reads and writes the target system automatically, for example over LDAP or JDBC, usually through the virtual appliance, as opposed to file uploads or manual handling.
Any system with no automated read and write connectivity, where updates are fulfilled by people through manual work items or helpdesk tickets rather than by a connector.
Customizable notification content, with Velocity variables for names and links, sent for events such as approvals, campaign launches or lifecycle changes; sender address and branding can also be set.
Protecting stored data such as databases, file stores and backups with strong ciphers like AES-256, so that copied or stolen storage yields nothing readable without the keys.
Protecting data moving between browsers, appliances, cloud services and target systems with TLS, so it cannot be read or altered by anyone intercepting network traffic.
The terminal node of an automation that marks its run as succeeded or failed; every branch needs one so execution history shows a clear outcome.
An access right on a connected system, such as a group, permission or license; it can be marked requestable or privileged, given an owner and description, and bundled into access profiles.
The job collecting groups, permissions and other access objects with their descriptions from a connected system, separate from collecting user records, so access can be described and assigned.
Automatically moving an overdue approval to a higher-level person, usually the approver's manager or a backup, after a set number of reminders or days, so requests do not stall.
A published platform occurrence, such as identity created, identity attributes changed or aggregation completed, that subscribers like HTTP endpoints or workflows receive in order to run automation.
A trust arrangement letting users sign in once with their home identity provider and reach applications in other domains via signed assertions, without separate passwords per app.
Returns the first non-null value from an ordered list of inputs, useful when an attribute may be empty on some systems and a fallback value should be used instead.
Collection that reads every account from a connected system each time; slower than collecting only changes, but needed to detect deletions reliably and correct drift.
Cloud-run code with no fixed calling context, typically invoked from a rule-type transform when declarative operations cannot produce the needed value.
A named set of identities acting together as approver or reviewer, where a decision by any one member completes the step, avoiding single points of delay.
Ongoing status checks reported for each appliance, cluster and connected system, such as connectivity, version and resource use, shown as healthy or unhealthy in the admin interface.
An administrative level for support staff that can view identities and assist users, for example with password and invitation tasks, without broad configuration rights.
Designing so service continues through component failure, for example several appliances per cluster spread across hosts or sites, backed by redundant SailPoint cloud services.
A person or non-human entity tracked by the tenant, built from authoritative account data and linked to all of its accounts on other systems, carrying attributes, a lifecycle state and access.
A named property on an identity, such as email, department, manager or cloudLifecycleState; standard ones exist by default and custom ones can be added and used in searches and criteria.
Configuration on an identity profile stating where each identity property gets its value, from a source account attribute, a transform or a rule, evaluated on every refresh.
A cloud-run script that computes an identity property with custom code when a transform cannot express the logic, attached through the identity profile's mappings.
Configuration tied to one authoritative source that turns its accounts into identities, defining attribute mappings, lifecycle states and priority; each identity is governed by exactly one.
A number deciding which configuration governs a person who has accounts on more than one authoritative source; the higher-priority profile wins.
The process that recalculates attributes, lifecycle state, role membership and resulting access for identities, run after aggregations and profile changes, nightly, or on demand.

SailPoint's multi-tenant SaaS governance platform, formerly IdentityNow, run and updated by SailPoint, reaching on-premises systems through virtual appliances and limiting custom code to reviewed rules.
Returns the current value of an existing identity property, commonly used inside provisioning policies to copy identity data into new account attributes.
SailPoint's customer-managed governance product, installed on the customer's own servers and broadly customizable with BeanShell, unlike the SaaS platform SailPoint runs and updates.
A lightweight Windows service on a domain member server that the appliance calls for Microsoft tasks needing native APIs, such as password changes, Exchange mailboxes and PowerShell after scripts.
Integration for relational databases that reads accounts and groups with SQL queries through a driver on the appliance, and makes changes with SQL, stored procedures or a provision rule.
Appliance-side code invoked by the database connector to carry out account creates, updates and deletes with custom SQL or stored procedures when standard statements are not enough.
A new person entering the organization; once they appear in the system of record they receive an identity and birthright access, ideally ready on their first day.
The secret set in an appliance's config.yaml that protects its private key; it must match across the cluster and be safeguarded, because losing it means re-entering source credentials.
Giving each user or service only the minimum access needed to do its job, for only as long as needed, limiting the damage from mistakes or compromise.
A person departing the organization, whose accounts must be disabled or removed promptly, typically driven by a terminated status or end date in the HR system.
Setting on an employment stage that enables or disables accounts on chosen systems whenever a person enters it, for example disabling every account when status becomes terminated.
A named employment stage such as prehire, active or inactive, defined per identity profile, which can enable or disable accounts, grant access profiles and send emails when entered.
Maps an input value to an output through a key-value table, such as converting department codes into department names, with a default entry for unmatched inputs.
Converts every character of an input string to lowercase, often applied to email addresses and usernames so they are formatted consistently.
A non-human actor such as a service account, bot or API client that holds access and needs an owner, reviews and lifecycle controls like a person does.
A review campaign where each manager decides whether direct reports should keep their current access; people with no manager need a fallback reviewer or are left out.
Settings that map a source account attribute, such as a supervisor's employee ID, to an identity attribute so each person's manager is found, enabling manager approvals and manager reviews.
A task assigned to a person, usually the source owner, to make a change by hand on a system that cannot be updated automatically, and then mark it complete.
Conditions on a role, built from identity attributes, account attributes or held entitlements, or a list of named identities, that decide who receives it automatically during refresh.
Platform design built from many small, independently deployed services, each owning one function such as search or provisioning, that talk over APIs and message queues and scale separately.
An existing person changing department, location or job, whose access should be adjusted to the new position while old access is removed to prevent accumulation.
A SaaS model where many customers run on shared cloud services and infrastructure while each customer's data is tagged, logically isolated and processed separately from everyone else's.
Support for one identity holding more than one account on the same source, such as standard and admin; requesters pick the target account and create profiles generate a distinct one.
A source setting that flags changes made directly on the target system outside the tenant, such as a group added by hand, so they can trigger events or workflows.
The unique key an account has on its own system, such as a distinguished name or employee number, used to track and target that account.
A contractor, vendor, partner or other external worker whose access must be governed with defined sponsors and end dates, often lacking an HR record.
An authorization framework in which a server issues scoped access tokens to client applications, so APIs can be called without ever sharing a user's password.
A label limiting what an access token may do, so an API client or personal token can be granted only the specific permissions a script needs instead of everything.
An identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 that adds an ID token describing the signed-in user, widely used for modern web and mobile sign-in.
Default behavior where the cloud skips processing accounts whose data is unchanged since the last collection, although the connector still reads them all, unlike a delta run.
The highest administrative level, with full control over every tenant setting, identity, source and API, so it should be limited to very few trusted people.
An account with no valid owner, often left behind after someone departs; a common audit finding that governance tools aim to detect and remove.
Letting people sign in to the tenant with existing directory credentials, checked live against a connected system such as Active Directory, instead of keeping a separate SailPoint password.
A client ID and secret tied to one user, inheriting that user's permissions and chosen scopes, which scripts exchange for an OAuth access token through the client credentials grant.
A detected case of someone holding conflicting access defined by a separation-of-duties rule, assigned to an owner who can remediate it or approve an exception with justification.
Evaluation during an access request that shows the requester and approvers when granting an item would create a separation-of-duties conflict, before access is granted.
Gradual buildup of unneeded access as people change jobs without old rights being removed, which mover processes and access reviews aim to prevent.
Access flagged as high-risk, such as domain admin group membership, so it is highlighted in reviews, easy to target with searches and given stricter approvals.
Creating, modifying, enabling, disabling or deleting accounts and access on target systems, triggered by requests, role changes, lifecycle changes, attribute sync or certification revocations.

An account operation that the connector or target rejected, shown with an error in account activity; common causes are bad credentials, missing required attributes or policy-generated duplicate values.
The internal instruction set listing account and attribute operations to send to a connector for one identity; rules and policies can inspect or alter it before execution.
Source configuration defining which attribute values to send for an operation type such as create, update, enable or disable; the create version is the one most often configured.
Optional appliance settings in a proxy.yaml file that route its outbound cloud traffic through a corporate web proxy, with exclusions so internal target systems are reached directly.
Calls another saved transform by its identifier and returns that result, letting common logic be defined once and reused inside many other definitions.
Removal of access a reviewer revoked in a campaign, carried out automatically through a connector or as a manual work item for disconnected systems, and tracked until complete.
An automated email nudging an approver or campaign reviewer who has not yet acted, sent at a configured interval until the item is decided or passed upward.
Finds text matching a regular expression in an input string and substitutes new text, such as stripping spaces, apostrophes or accented characters from names.
The end-user portal where people browse and ask for access for themselves or others, follow pending requests and see their status.
An event subscription type where the tenant waits for the subscriber's reply and can act on it, such as an external approval decision, unlike fire-and-forget delivery that only notifies.
A flag that makes an access profile, role or entitlement appear in Request Center so users can ask for it, subject to segments and approvals.
The HTTP interface that exposes tenant functions as resources with JSON payloads and versioned paths such as v3 and beta, used for scripting, automation and integration with other tools.

A business-level bundle of access profiles and entitlements that may span several sources, assigned by membership criteria or request; unlike an access profile it models a job function, not one system's access.
A review campaign where role owners confirm each role still contains the right access profiles and entitlements and its criteria are still valid, rather than reviewing individual people.

Custom Java BeanShell code that extends behavior where configuration falls short; unlike a declarative JSON transform it is procedural, and it executes either in SailPoint's cloud or on the appliance.
A JSON definition that hands its input to a generic cloud rule and returns the code's output, used when logic is too complex for declarative operations.
SailPoint's command-line tool that scans BeanShell code for disallowed classes and risky patterns before it is uploaded or submitted, catching problems before deployment.
A cloud-hosted integration that reaches internet-facing applications straight from SailPoint's cloud with no virtual appliance, built on the newer connectivity framework.
The built-in Linux account used to sign in to an appliance over SSH or the console for diagnostics; its default password must be changed at first login.
A separate non-production instance used to build and test transforms, rules, workflows and other changes safely before promoting the configuration to the production instance.
A stored query with chosen columns and filters that can be rerun from the search page and reused as the basis for scheduled email reports or search-based review campaigns.
A recurring timer on a connected system that runs its account or group collection automatically, for instance nightly, so changes reach the tenant without manual starts.
A review campaign whose population comes from a query, such as everyone holding privileged entitlements, letting administrators target a precise slice of access.
An Elasticsearch-style expression such as attributes.department:Finance AND NOT attributes.cloudLifecycleState:inactive, used to find identities, access items, accounts or events across the tenant.
A schedule attached to a stored query that emails its results as a CSV attachment to chosen recipients daily, weekly or monthly, optionally only when results exist.
A visibility scope that limits which access items particular users can see and request, based on identity criteria; it controls what is displayed, not what someone already holds.
Sends account changes as tickets to an ITSM tool such as ServiceNow and polls their status, so a help desk team carries out changes on systems without direct connectivity.
A separation-of-duties definition listing two conflicting sets of access, such as creating vendors and approving payments, so holders of both are flagged in requests, reviews and reports.
A connected system, such as HR, a directory, database or SaaS app, configured in the tenant with a connector, from which accounts and entitlements are collected and where changes are made.
An indicator on each connected system showing whether recent connection tests and collections succeeded, used to spot expired credentials, broken network paths or offline appliances.
The identity accountable for a connected system, who may approve requests for its access, review its accounts in campaigns and receive manual work items for it.
A review campaign where the owner of each selected system evaluates every account and entitlement on it, regardless of which manager the account holders report to.
An administrative level scoped through governance groups to particular connected systems, letting delegated staff manage only those systems' settings, aggregations and access profiles.
A review campaign generated but not yet activated, letting administrators preview reviewers and items and catch data problems such as missing managers before anyone is notified.
Returns a fixed value or a Velocity-template expression built from other inputs, useful for constants or for combining several results with simple template logic.
Extracts part of a string using begin and end index positions, such as taking the first letter of a first name when building a username.
An organization's own isolated instance of the SailPoint cloud service, reached at a unique subdomain and holding its identities, sources, policies and configuration apart from other customers.
The cloud geography, for example US, EU or Asia-Pacific, where an organization's instance and data are hosted, chosen at purchase for latency and data-residency requirements.
The web address of an organization's instance, in the form company.identitynow.com for the user interface, while REST calls go to the matching company.api.identitynow.com host.
A source action verifying that the appliance can reach and authenticate to the target with the saved settings; the first troubleshooting step when collection or changes fail.

A reusable JSON object that reshapes data, such as formatting dates, joining names or mapping codes, without writing code; unlike a rule it is declarative and customers manage it themselves through the API.
An account that could not be matched to any identity during aggregation; on a non-authoritative system it stays unowned until linked manually or the matching logic is fixed.
An administrative permission set assigned to an identity, such as Admin, Helpdesk, Source Sub-Admin or Role Admin, controlling which admin pages and APIs it may use.
Used in a create provisioning policy to try a series of candidate patterns, checking each for uniqueness on the target system, until an unused account name is found.
A group of appliances serving the same sources and sharing work and keys, so that if one fails the others carry on; at least two members are recommended for availability.
Public and private keys generated for an appliance cluster; source passwords typed into the UI are encrypted with the public key so that only the appliance can decrypt them.
The appliance needs outbound TLS on port 443 to SailPoint's cloud, working DNS, accurate time and reach to its target systems; no inbound internet firewall openings are required.
Automatic patching in which SailPoint pushes operating system and connector service updates to appliances, so customers normally do not upgrade them by hand; members may reboot as needed.
Apache templating syntax supported in static transforms and email content to build values from variables, conditions and string methods.
A Linux-based virtual machine deployed in the customer's network that hosts connector services, reaches on-premises systems, and talks to the SaaS service using only outbound HTTPS.
A configurable integration that calls a target's REST or SOAP endpoints through defined HTTP operations, with paging and response mapping, for applications lacking a dedicated connector.
An HTTP endpoint registered to receive event payloads as JSON POST calls, secured with basic or bearer authentication, so external systems can react to tenant events.
Delegating approvals and other pending tasks from one identity to another for a date range, for example during leave, so work keeps moving without sharing credentials.
A low-code automation assembled in a visual editor that starts from a trigger and runs actions and operators, for example emailing a manager when someone's department changes.
An automation step that performs work, such as getting identity details, managing access, creating a certification, sending an email or making an HTTP request to another system.
The record of each automation run showing its trigger input, step outputs, status and errors, which is the first place to look when troubleshooting a failed or unexpected run.
A logic step that controls flow rather than doing work, such as comparing strings or numbers, verifying data types, looping or waiting, deciding which branch an automation follows.
The starting point of an automation: a platform event, a schedule, an external call or a manual launch, which supplies the input data available to every later step.
